In Level 2, UP/DOWN does nothing. LEFT/RIGHT moves the gray piece by 6. In other words, in this level, only horizontal movement of the gray piece is possible.
Gray piece: rows 18–29, top bar is columns 15–23, bottom bar is columns 9–17.
Yellow: rows 42–53, top bar is columns 9–17, bottom bar is columns 3–11.
If the gray can only move horizontally, it can never reach the yellow (different rows). So the goal must be something else. What can the gray do? Move horizontally by 6: the top bar's columns are 15, 9, 3, or 21, 27, 33…
Hmm, wait — maybe the goal is to align the gray piece with the black piece's mirror image, or to align the gray piece with the black piece's column? Or maybe the goal is related to the white dots on the divider (separator line)?
Let me think about the game from a different angle. Level 1: the black piece (player) moves in all directions, the gray mirror follows, and the goal = the mirror overlaps with the yellow. Level 2: the gray piece is the player (moves only horizontally, 6 per step?), and the black is a static template. Goal = ???
Actually, wait. Maybe I should reconsider: the gray piece moves 6 per step because it's the mirror of the black piece, and the black piece is what's being moved… but the black didn't move. No, that's not it.
Or maybe the gray piece is the player piece, and it moves 6 per step horizontally. The goal is to line up the gray piece with something. What's at the same row as the gray (rows 18–29)? The black piece is at rows 18–29, columns 45–59 (right side). The divider is at columns 36–38. The left region is columns 0–35.
If the gray moves right: the top bar's columns are 15→21→27→33. At 33, the gray's top bar is at 33–41? No wait, the gray's top bar is 9 wide: 33–41 would cross the divider (36–38). Hmm, the gray's shape: top bar 9 wide, bottom bar 9 wide, offset by 6. If the top bar is at 33–41, it crosses the divider. Maybe it gets blocked there.
Hmm, what's the goal? Maybe the goal is to align the gray piece's mirror image (which would appear on the right side) with the black template? The black is at columns 45–59 (top 45–53, bottom 51–59). The gray's mirror: c' = 74−c. If the gray's top bar is at columns 15–23 → mirror is 51–59; bottom bar 9–17 → mirror is 57–65. The black's top bar is 45–53, bottom bar is 51–59. Not aligned.
For the gray's mirror to match the black: the gray's top bar's mirror = 45–53 → the gray's top bar is at 74−53=21 to 74−45=29 → 21–29. The gray's bottom bar's mirror = 51–59 → the gray's bottom bar is at 74−59=15 to 74−51=23 → 15–23. So the gray's top bar 21–29, bottom bar 15–23. That's exactly the gray's initial position (before I moved it)! At the start of Level 2, the gray was at top 21–29, bottom 15–23, and its mirror was exactly the black's position.
So at the start of the level, the gray's mirror was already overlapping with the black. I moved the gray 6 to the left (top 15–23, bottom 9–17), and the mirror is now at top 51–59, bottom 57–65 — no longer overlapping with the black.
Hmm, so the goal isn't "align the mirror with the black" (it was already aligned at the start).
Let me think again… Maybe the goal is to align the gray piece with the yellow piece. But the gray can only move horizontally, and the yellow is 24 rows below. Impossible.
Maybe SPACE or ACTION7 or MOUSE does something — like rotating the piece or toggling something. Let me try SPACE and ACTION7 and see what happens.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the movement. Maybe the gray piece moves 6 per step horizontally, and the black piece moves 6 per step vertically? But the black didn't move on DOWN. Hmm, DOWN was pressed 3 times total, and the black didn't move.
Or maybe the arrow keys move the piece on the side you're pressing toward? LEFT moves the left piece (gray) to the left, RIGHT moves the left piece to the right?? That would be weird. Actually, RIGHT moved the gray 6 to the right (9→15). So both LEFT and RIGHT move the gray (the left piece). What about the black (the right piece)? Maybe the black moves with… hmm, both LEFT and RIGHT moved the gray. So the arrow keys control the gray regardless of direction.
So in Level 2: the gray piece is the player, and it moves horizontally by 6 per step. UP/DOWN do nothing (or they're for a different piece that's currently locked).
What's the goal? Maybe: move the gray piece so its mirror overlaps with the black piece? At the start it was already overlapping… unless the level started in a non-overlapping state and I'm misremembering. At the start of Level 2 (after the Level 1 batch), the gray was at top 21–29 (boundary [[18,21],[18,29]]), and the black was at top 45–53. Mirror of gray top 21–29 = 45–53 ✓. Gray bottom 15–23 → mirror 51–59 = black bottom ✓. So it was overlapping from the start. Weird as a goal.
Maybe the goal is to align the gray piece with the yellow piece's column? The yellow's top bar is 9–17, bottom bar is 3–11. If the gray's top bar is at 9–17 (bottom bar 3–11), the gray's column layout matches the yellow's. That's the position I just reached! (Top 15–23? No wait.) Let me check: after LEFT2, the gray's top bar was at 9–17 (boundary [[18,9],[18,17]]). Then RIGHT brought it back to 15–23. Hmm, so currently the gray's top is 15–23, bottom is 9–17. The yellow's top is 9–17, bottom is 3–11. So to match the yellow's columns, the gray needs one more LEFT (top 9–17, bottom 3–11).
But why would that be the goal? Maybe the goal is to drop the gray onto the yellow… but DOWN doesn't work.
Hmm, let me try SPACE and ACTION7. Maybe SPACE "drops" the piece, or toggles the movement axis. Let me investigate.
